Subject: FY27 inference budget — prepay options and timing

Hi Marissa,

We're kicking off FY27 planning and I need a budgetary quote for an annual prepay scenario. Stratus is evaluating a 3-year commitment but would like to see two alternatives: 1) annual prepay with escalator, 2) 3-year committed prepay with a ramp schedule (year 1 lower usage, year 3 full run-rate).

Key ask: line-item pro forma for each year showing unit price, term discount, and recommended ramp. We also want a plug for an early-payment discount if we prepay >70% in year 1. Goal is to have a pro forma to take to finance by 3/10.

Can you share a budgetary pro forma and any packaging guidance (e.g., reserved vs hosted tier recommendations) by EOD Monday?

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Procurement
Stratus Analytics

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a first-pass pro forma and two ramp scenarios (Option A: conservative ramp; Option B: aggressive ramp) plus short notes on packaging trade-offs. Highlights up front:

- 1-year annual prepay: suitable if you want flexibility; we can offer a 12% prepay discount on published hosted rates for a 1-year prepay at >50% commitment.
- 3-year committed prepay: we can structure a step-down unit price with an aggregate term discount (example below).
- Early-payment add-on: additional 3% effective discount if >70% invoice paid at contract signature for Year 1.

I've looped in Dylan for technical sizing recommendations and Stephanie for approval on any non-standard commercial terms. If these look reasonable, I can produce a formal pro forma (Excel) and a short SOW stub for procurement.

Quick technical note on sizing and packaging:

- For Stratus' projected mix (30% embeddings, 60% chat/generation, 10% reranking), we recommend Dedicated pool with reserved capacity for predictable latency and cheaper unit economics when prepaying.
- Year 1 conservative: 60% of target vCPU/GPU utilization — use reserved + burst capacity.
- Year 3 full run-rate: target continuous capacity, quantify as reserved with autoscale headroom.

If Marissa is proposing the pricing tiers in the spreadsheet, the ramp shapes map to GPU-hours in tab "Sizing". Happy to run a quick re-size if they share expected monthly token volumes.

Thanks Marissa and Dylan — this is helpful. A couple clarifying items from finance/internal procurement:

1) Can you show the pro forma with and without the early-payment add-on so we can present both scenarios?
2) For the 3-year term, can you include an annual true-up clause and proposed crediting approach if actual usage falls below commitment?
3) Any calendar impact for revenue recognition? Finance prefers even amortization over the period.

If you include those, we'll be comfortable presenting to our CFO on 3/10. We're leaning toward the 3-year committed if the aggregate term discount reaches ~22% effective vs hosted list across the three years.

Elena — thanks, great direction. I've updated the pro forma to include columns: (A) list-hosted pricing baseline, (B) 1-year prepay scenario (12% discount), (C) 3-year committed ramp scenario (year1: 8% discount, year2: 18% discount, year3: 28% discount cumulative), and (D) 3-year with early-payment add-on (extra 3% in year1). Marissa/Elena — I reviewed the proposed commercial approach. High level: the quarterly true-up with a 12-month window for credits is operationally simpler and acceptable from a revenue recognition perspective if we: (1) document the amortization approach in the contract, and (2) do not allow credits to be converted into cash refunds. That said, finance will require the contract to state even amortization of the prepaid consideration for external reporting; we can do the operational quarterly reconciliation as you suggested.

Marissa: please proceed with ProForma v2 that includes both "with early pay" and "without early pay" columns, and add a short clause for quarterly true-up + 12-month crediting. Once we have that, Elena, you should be able to take this to CFO.
